bullets.title: MRVL +21% premarket: Jensen Huang calls it 'next $1T company'
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang explicitly called Marvell 'the next trillion-dollar company' at Computex/GTC Taipei, reportedly saying it twice and ending with 'buy Marvell.' MRVL surged ~17-21% in after-hours/premarket, with current market cap cited at ~$191B—implying ~5x upside in Jensen's framing. Multiple fintwit accounts flagged MRVL as a mainstream beneficiary of NVLink and the network stack buildout.

bullets.title: Alphabet raises $80B for AI capex; Berkshire invests $10B
bullets.body: Google announced an $80B equity capital raise for AI infrastructure: $40B via ATM offering, $30B in underwritten/convertible preferred offerings, and a $10B strategic investment from Berkshire Hathaway. 2026 CapEx guided at $190B with 2027 expected to increase significantly. GOOGL fell ~2% AH on dilution concerns despite bullish strategic read-throughs for the semiconductor supply chain (LITE, AVGO, TSM, MU cited by multiple accounts).

bullets.title: HPE surges 30-33% AH on massive EPS guide raise; AI server demand through FY27
bullets.body: HPE Q2 revenue beat at $10.68B vs. $9.79B est (+40% YoY); raised FY adjusted EPS guidance to $3.35-$3.45 vs. $2.43 consensus. Networks-for-AI FY2026 order target raised to $2B+. Management signaled demand strength continues through fiscal 2027, with Q3 EPS guided $0.88-0.93 vs. $0.58 est. Trader commentary flagged potential dotcom-era valuation stretch vs. genuine AI infrastructure demand signal.

bullets.title: NVDA adds $319B in market cap; CEO highlights Vera demand, China sales, FCF return
bullets.body: NVIDIA shares closed +6.3%, adding $319B in market cap. Jensen Huang flagged: (1) Vera demand likely to exceed GPU lineup; (2) adequate supply for robust CPU/GPU growth; (3) U.S. approval to sell chips in China with full compliance commitment; (4) plan to return 50%+ of FCF to shareholders; (5) preference for off-the-shelf ARM designs over custom CPU cores. ARK Invest bought 300K NVDA shares and sold 110K AMD shares on the day.

bullets.title: Computex CPO supply chain mapped: Wiwynn/AyarLabs/Lumentum; LITE as laser supplier
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts at Computex Taiwan highlighted the emerging CPO supply chain: Wiwynn (NVIDIA's ODM rack partner) displayed CPO AI Accelerator using AyarLabs TeraPHY optical engine. Lumentum/LITE flagged as one of only two public laser suppliers alongside GFS-partnered Sivers for CPO and pluggable applications. One account noted a LITE breakout could trigger a bid across the infrastructure sector. Separately, IC substrate surface area projected to triple, seen as tailwind for substrate manufacturers.

bullets.title: MRVL interconnect bottleneck thesis; Google/Marvell CXL-pooled DRAM; STX KV cache offload
bullets.body: One fintwit account noted Marvell management has been discussing interconnect bottleneck as a key constraint in AI infrastructure. Separately, Google is reportedly designing an MPU with Marvell to access CXL-pooled DRAM for HBF exploration, while Nvidia is offloading KV cache to SSDs through Seagate's STX system while keeping weights in HBM.

bullets.title: MediaTek at Goldman Sachs Taiwan Day: exclusive EMIB-T for next-gen chip, tape-out 4Q26
bullets.body: MediaTek confirmed at Goldman Sachs Taiwan Day that its next-generation program adopts only EMIB-T packaging (not mixed CoWoS as previously reported), with tape-out targeted 4Q26 and mass production 4Q27. Intel's EMIB-T also gained traction as Google qualified the tech for TPU v8t (Zebrafish), driven by CoWoS capacity shortages at TSMC—potentially reducing TSM advanced packaging dependency.

bullets.title: DRAM prices up 58-63% Q2 vs Q1; MU market cap crosses $1 trillion
bullets.body: TrendForce projects mainstream DRAM contract prices up 58-63% in Q2 vs Q1 (following 93-98% surge in Q1), with supplier inventory at extremely low levels and AI demand accelerating. Micron's market cap surpassed $1 trillion, up 10x over the past year. SNDK also flagged with a 99 RSI and MU monthly RSI above 90—fintwit commentary noting extreme overbought signals.

bullets.title: CRDO Q4 beats; Q1 guided above consensus; AI bottleneck shifting to network reliability
bullets.body: Credo Technology Q1 revenue guidance of $465M-$475M beat $460.5M consensus; gross margin guided 67-69%. Earnings call read-through: AI infrastructure bottleneck shifting from raw accelerator availability toward network reliability and power efficiency. Copper business described as core growth engine with AEC adoption extending to multi-rack deployments.

bullets.title: HOOD: $20M insider buy; WonderFi acquisition closed; bullish technical setup
bullets.body: HOOD director Meyer Malka purchased $20M in shares via Bullfrog Capital, the first insider buy in one year. Robinhood also closed its acquisition of WonderFi, entering the Canadian market. Multiple fintwit accounts noted HOOD forming a bullish technical base with divergence on the weekly chart, held from $75.87 entry by one trader, though volume confirmation still awaited.

bullets.title: S&P 500 hits 7,600 for first time; 23rd ATH in 2026; but breadth narrow
bullets.body: S&P 500 crossed 7,600 for the first time (up 28% YoY, 81% over 5 years) extending its winning streak to 8 sessions, with 23 all-time highs in 2026. Fintwit flagged narrow market breadth: over 50% of S&P 500 stocks trade below their 100-day MA, only tech and energy sectors green on the day. Options put/call ratio hit 0.64, a 5-year bullish extreme, and hedge funds bought equities at the fastest pace of 2024.

bullets.title: TSLA -4.6% on SPCX dilution fears; institutional pushback on conglomerate structure
bullets.body: Tesla fell 4.6% vs NDX +0.6% as SPCX filed an amended S-1/A suggesting more SPCX equity issuance potentially linked to a Tesla acquisition. Multiple accounts note institutional investors dislike the proposed TSLA-SPCX combination due to dilution concerns and preference for pure-play exposure; clearing the deal could act as a re-rating catalyst.

bullets.title: Alphabet's $80B raise: dilution concern vs. strategic bullishness on TPU ecosystem
bullets.body: Fintwit split on GOOGL AH reaction: bears flagged dilution (stock down 2% AH) and one commentator noted capex of ~$185B projected against ~$74B FCF may require ongoing capital raises. Bulls cited $174B operating cash flow generated in past 12 months and framed the raise as confirmatory for the broader TPU supply chain. Berkshire's $10B private placement seen as endorsement of GOOGL's long-term value.

bullets.title: INTC: U.S. government took 9.9% stake in Aug 2025; Q1 2026 beat sent stock +22% premarket
bullets.body: One account detailed that the U.S. government took a 9.9% stake in Intel at $20.47/share in August 2025; Intel subsequently beat Q1 2026 earnings on every line, sending the stock up 22% in a single pre-market session. Intel also showcased chip-to-rackscale AI solutions at Computex with partner support.

bullets.title: NBIS: €8B French AI cloud investment announced; exposure to META and MSFT
bullets.body: Macron announced Nebius is investing €8B to build AI cloud infrastructure in France. Separately, one account noted NBIS has exposure to META and MSFT as customers, and flagged GOOGL pursuing multiple Fluidstack colocation deals to expand TPU capacity. NBIS also hit another all-time high during the session.

bullets.title: MDB up 30%; 'Netflix of the cloud' thesis; CRWV +14%; SNOW investor day tomorrow
bullets.body: One trader flagged MDB up 30%+ with volume picking up, holding position and expecting breakout to all-time highs under a 'Netflix of the cloud / AI can't kill software' thesis. CRWV surged 14% with trader watching for follow-through. Snowflake hosts investor day Tuesday morning alongside two Fed speaker appearances.

bullets.title: RGTI valuation gap vs. peers flagged: $90/forward sales dollar vs. Infleqtion
bullets.body: One account noted RGTI trades at ~$90 per forward dollar of sales despite generating only $4.4M in revenue last quarter vs. Infleqtion's $9.5M—a stark valuation gap for nearly identical sector narratives. Commentary framed as a cautionary note on quantum name valuations.

bullets.title: BOJ signals June rate hike; SMFG exec calls for action; JGB yields fall on auction
bullets.body: Bank of Japan strengthened arguments for a June rate hike with one participant advocating nimble emergency bond-buying if markets destabilize. SMFG's Global Markets Chief called for a June BOJ rate increase, while proposing 2.1 trillion yen monthly bond purchases from April 2027. Japan's 10-year JGB yield fell 10 bps to 2.58% following a strong bond auction.

bullets.title: EU trade deal advances; ECB Rabobank +25bp hike Sept; gold replaces Treasuries as top reserve
bullets.body: EU Parliament trade committee voted to remove duties on many U.S. goods ahead of Trump's July 4 deadline; EU lawmakers cleared the deal for final approval. Rabobank forecasts an additional 25bp ECB hike, most likely in September. The ECB separately reported gold has surpassed U.S. Treasuries as the world's top reserve asset. 10-year Treasuries fell 4.9 bps to 4.428%.

bullets.title: Consumer credit stress: delinquencies at multi-year highs across all categories
bullets.body: Q1 2026 data shows U.S. consumer loan delinquencies hit a 9-year high at 4.8% (30+ days past due). Credit card serious delinquencies rose to 13.1%—highest since Q4 2010 and approaching the 2008 peak of 13.7%. Auto loan serious delinquencies hit a record 5.6%. Student loan 90+ day delinquencies jumped 70 bps to 10.3%, the highest since Q1 2020.
